messages:
Maya: heads up — saw a p99 spike on prod around 21:30 UTC in the eu-west pool after the kernel-selection roll at ~21:15. p95 flat, p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s when concurrency > ~600. looks correlated with KV cache eviction churn

Ravi: same here. digged into logs, lot of repeated kv_eviction::evict_and_wake loops. hitrate drops from 92% -> 60% under load. interestingly requests that hit eviction path get an extra 800-1200ms.

Sam: flamegraph quicklink: https://perf.internal/fg/172345 — top stacks show heavy time in eviction_lock and kernel_switch_async. suggests we might be thrashing between kernels when cache misses spike.

Priya: can we confirm this is the kernel-selection change and not a microbatch config change? I don't see MB config flips in the deploy diff but could be an interaction.

Maya: deploy diff was just kernel policy tweak: "kernel_policy: latency-preferring" (instead of throughput-preferring). no MB changes. snippet from the rollout config: ```json
{"kernel_policy":"latency-preferring","sticky_kernel":false,"mb_target":16}
```

Ravi: here's a small repro on staging I ran: `wrk -c 800 -t 16 -d 60s --timeout 10s /v1/generate` — p95 ~240ms, p99 ~980ms when I force kv.hotset to 40%. CLI output: ```
SUMMARY: requests: 120k, p95: 240ms, p99: 980ms, kv_hits: 48%
```

Sam: hypothesis: with latency-preferring kernels we switch kernels more aggressively for short sequences; that plus low KV hit rate causes frequent kernel handoff and eviction work (locks/contention). The handoff cost shows up only at tail.

Priya: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) reduce mb_target from 16 -> 8 to lower contention, 2) add hysteresis to kv-evict so we don't start evicting at transient dips. both low-risk to test in canary.

Maya: agreed. also trying sticky_kernel=true to avoid kernel churn. config to test (canary): ```json
{"kernel_policy":"latency-preferring","sticky_kernel":true,"mb_target":8,"kv_evict_hysteresis_ms":500}
```

perf-bot: alert: high-p99 observed on service-inference (eu-west) at 2024-06-18T21:30:12Z — see thread for investigation.

Ravi: also suggested bumping per-worker cache sharding from 4 -> 6 to reduce lock contention; cheap if memory headroom exists. if hitrate remains low, scaling cache smaller isn't helpful but increasing shards helps concurrency.

Sam: another quick experiment: keep mb_target=16 but gate microbatching when kv_miss_rate > 30% (i.e., force single-request path). avoids batching churn when cache is cold.

Priya: I'll run two canaries: A) sticky_kernel + mb_target=8 + hysteresis; B) mb_target=16 + kv_miss_gate. collect p95/p99 and kv_hitrate. will run for 30m each.

Maya: thanks. also adding a trace point to measure kernel_switch_count per-request and kv_eviction_duration so we can correlate.

Ravi: if canary A improves p99 by >30% without throughput regression we'll roll. if not, revert kernel-policy change immediately.

Sam: note for follow-up — profiling shows eviction_lock held ~25-40ms per eviction call under high concurrency. that was not visible at low qps.

Maya: schedule: Priya starts canaries in 15m, I'll watch dashboards and collect flamegraphs. tagging @oncall in case of regression. :thumbsup:

Priya: got it — kicking off canary A now. will post results in ~35m.

Ravi: thanks — also add a perf regression test in CI: synthetic KV churn workload to catch this before next rollout.

Sam: +1 to CI test. small followup: consider making kernel switch async-without-lock to reduce blocking path but that's a larger runtime change. will add to backlog.

Maya: good notes. leaving this thread open until we have canary numbers.
